newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S PACTUAL BOUGHT CREDIREAL FOR BCN.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S PACTUAL BOUGHT CREDIREAL FOR BCN.

text.p: Brazil's Banco Pactual bought Minas Gerais state bank Credireal for local private bank BCN at Thursday's privatization auction, Minas Gerais Finance Secretary Joao Heraldo Lima said.
"Banco Pactual confirmed it bought Credireal for BCN," Lima told reporters.
BCN was represented by Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana, a company created by Pactual to look into opportunities in Brazil's banking sector for local and foreign investors.
BCN acquired Credireal for the bank's base price of 121.3 million reais at a closed-envelope auction on the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB).

The bank was the only investor to place bids. The other two investors scheduled to participate in the auction -- Banco Industrial e Comercial (Bicbanco) and Varejo S.A. Administracao e Participacao, a unit of local Bozano, Simonsen group -- declined to present offers.
Outgoing Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola said the Credireal sale was successful, even though only one investor placed bids, as the bank was sold 30 percent above its net worth value.
Minas Gerais state Finance Secretary said the winning bidder is due to pay cash for Credireal on August 12.
Lima said the state will use the money raised with the Credireal sale to pay off debts owed to the federal government.
He also said the state would appeal a court order requesting the privatization revenue be used to pay off workers-related debts.
Credireal was the second Brazilian state-owned bank to be privatized. The first was Rio de Janeiro state bank Banco Banerj SA, which was bought by Brazil's Banco Itau in June.
